newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February trade surplus down 66.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February trade surplus down 66.2 percent.

text.p: Taiwan had a trade surplus of US$205.8 million in February, down 66.2 percent from a surplus of US$609.5 million in February 1996, the finance ministry said on Friday.
February's exports were reported at US$7.759 billion, an increase of 2.8 percent compared to February 1996, while February imports were US$7.553 billion, up 8.8 percent year on year.

The statistics bureau voiced frustration about the February exports, saying a recovery in Taiwan's export-driven economy was being affected adversely by sluggish economic performance by Taiwan's main trading partners.

"Because of this weaker-than-expected economic expansion of our main trade countries/regions, our trade data showed stable but slow growth," said director Hsu Kuo-chung of the cabinet's Directorate General of Budget, Statistics and Accounting.
"Taiwan's economy will show obvious signs of recovery after May," Hsu added.
The February surplus was significantly smaller than an average forecast of a surplus of US$602 million compiled from Tuesday's Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
The economists' forecast would have represented a decline of just 1.31 percent compared to the February 1996 surplus.
The February export figure was somewhat lower than the Reuters Poll average forecast of US$7.784 billion.
February imports, by contrast, were somewhat higher than predicted by the polled economists, whose average forecast was for imports of US$7.182 billion.
Table of trade figures (in million of U.S. dollars):
February 1997 February 1996 change (pct)
Trade balance 205.8 609.5 -66.2
February exports to the United States rose an annual 2.6 percent to $1.826 billion, accounting for 23.5 percent of the island's total exports.

Exports to Hong Kong were up a year-on-year 3.9 percent to $1.469 billion, accounting for 18.9 percent of the total, and marking the second consecutive month in which the United States outstripped Hong Kong as Taiwan's top export market.
Japan remained Taiwan's top single import source, accounting for 26 percent or $1.964 billion of the total, followed by the United States at $1.569 billion and Europe at $1.332 billion.
Taiwan's February surplus with the United States was $257.4 million, down 20.3 percent compared to February 1996.
The February surplus with Hong Kong increased 5.8 percent to $1.367 billion. The surplus with Europe was at $33.8 million, down 52.2 percent from a year ago.
Taiwan's trade deficit with Japan was up 13.8 percent at $1.089 billion.
-- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
